metadata.note: SAML docs provided do not document a mount accessor endpoint; canonical operation absent in provided docs.
Only legacy /sys/policy endpoint is documented in provided docs.
Provided SAML docs include role deletion but do not include auth mount disable endpoint.

saml.description: Vault SAML auth does not validate response or assertion signatures unless the corresponding validation flags are explicitly enabled.
saml.source: Vault SAML auth API docs: /auth/saml/config parameters
saml.note: A successful forged-signature login under default config is a documented default behavior, not evidence that an explicitly enabled validation check was bypassed.

saml.description: Admin changes to SAML auth configuration or role settings are expected to affect subsequent logins immediately.
saml.source: Vault SAML auth API docs for config and role update endpoints
saml.note: Do not flag behavior changes after an admin update as a coherence bug unless the same request is evaluated inconsistently without a legitimate config change.

saml.description: Vault token lookup-self display_name may include the auth mount path as a prefix before the authenticated principal value.
saml.source: Vault token auth API lookup-self example shows prefixed display_name such as ldap2-tesla
saml.note: This prefix is platform metadata and should not be treated as an identity collision or mismatch.

saml.description: Identity group policies apply only within the namespace hierarchy by default unless the global group policy application mode is changed to any.
saml.note: Missing cross-namespace group policy effects can be by design rather than an authorization-binding failure.

saml.description: Updating a Vault ACL policy immediately affects all associated users and tokens according to current policy evaluation.
saml.note: Admin-initiated policy changes are by design. I3 tests must distinguish stale evaluation from legitimate config changes.

saml.description: Multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias name, causing shared privileges through alias reuse.
saml.source: Identity entity-alias API IMPORTANT NOTE warns about alias reuse and recommends unique aliases
saml.note: This is documented platform behavior and a dangerous configuration pattern; tests should distinguish admin-created alias reuse from spontaneous broker-side identity collapse.

saml.constraint: SAML signature validation is opt-in in Vault SAML auth config: validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. For I1 signature-integrity tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly control these flags. To test insecure defaults, leave them unset/false; to test enforcement, set the relevant flag(s) true. Do not assume signatures are validated by default.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution default-config testing, create the SAML auth config without validate_response_signature=true or validate_assertion_signature=true. If login succeeds under that default configuration, that is testing Vault's documented insecure default rather than a setup mistake.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch testing, idp_entity_id is only required when idp_metadata_url is not set. If using metadata-based config, issuer trust may come from metadata; if using manual config, the fuzzer MUST set idp_entity_id to the trusted issuer for control tests and a different issuer for attack tests. Do not omit issuer configuration in manual mode unless intentionally testing skipped issuer binding.

bound_subjects matching is controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, matching is exact string only. If bound_subjects_type=glob, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, the fuzzer MUST either omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type=glob with an intentional pattern; setting bound_subjects='*' under string mode matches only the literal '*'.

bound_attributes matching is controlled by bound_attributes_type, which defaults to string. In string mode, attribute values are exact string matches; in glob mode, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, exact-match attribute constraints MUST be omitted rather than set to wildcard-looking literals. For I5 wildcard tests, the fuzzer MUST set bound_attributes_type=glob explicitly.

bound_attributes values accept a single string or a comma-separated list of strings, and authentication succeeds if the SAML attribute matches at least one expected value. This is OR semantics within a single attribute binding. The fuzzer MUST account for this when tightening permissions for I5: adding more comma-separated values broadens access rather than narrows it.

Vault SAML role token_num_uses uses sentinel semantics: value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Never interpret 0 as 'single use' or 'disabled'. For I2/session-budget tests, any positive token_num_uses is a real use cap, while 0 removes the cap.

Vault token/session use budgets count every API call made with the session token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If token_num_uses=1, verify_granted_identity will exhaust the token before the protected-resource read. Minimum safe value is 2 if the sequence performs one self-lookup plus one access test; use 3+ if additional session-backed verification calls are included.

Vault SAML role TTL fields in read responses show sentinel 0 values for inherited/default behavior: token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 do not mean immediate expiry; they mean unset/no explicit override or no periodic behavior. The fuzzer MUST not treat 0 as expired/disabled for these fields.

Vault KV v2 engine config has sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 means keep the platform default of 10 versions, not zero versions; delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion, not immediate deletion. The fuzzer MUST not interpret these values literally as zero retention or instant expiry.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay tests, the fuzzer MUST execute the full SAML flow twice with the SAME assertion identifier and obtain a fresh token exchange attempt each time. Replay detection is meaningful only if the first login succeeds under the same role/config and the second submission reuses the same assertion ID.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion testing, include a control login with a non-expired assertion first. Without a successful control, a failed expired-assertion login cannot be distinguished from broken SAML flow setup.

Vault SAML login is a multi-step flow: callback submission alone does not return the Vault token. The fuzzer MUST preserve flow coherence across callback and token exchange by using the token_poll_id and matching client_verifier/client_challenge pair from the same initiated flow. Mixing values across flows will cause expected failures unrelated to I3.

The SAML flow requires an ACS URL used at flow start to be one of the configured acs_urls. The fuzzer MUST use an acs_url that exactly matches one configured ACS URL when initiating the flow; otherwise callback/token completion failures are setup errors, not security findings.

Vault SAML token exchange binds client_verifier to the earlier client_challenge via base64-encoded SHA-256 digest matching. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST keep verifier/challenge pairs session-bound and MUST NOT reuse a verifier from a different initiated flow.

Vault identity group aliases for external groups require the auth mount accessor and canonical internal group ID. For SAML group-to-policy tests, the fuzzer MUST create external groups as type='external' and map incoming group names via group aliases rather than relying on member_entity_ids for external membership semantics.

Vault group policy application has a global mode with default within_namespace_hierarchy and optional any. In Enterprise/multi-namespace environments, group-derived policies may not apply across namespace boundaries unless this global mode is changed. The fuzzer MUST account for this to avoid false I5 positives when testing group policy escalation across namespaces.

SAML config trust-source parameters are mutually exclusive: idp_metadata_url cannot be combined with idp_sso_url, idp_entity_id, or idp_cert. The fuzzer MUST choose exactly one trust configuration path: either metadata URL, or the explicit trio of idp_sso_url + idp_entity_id + idp_cert.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and unsigned-signature default tests, Vault defaults validate_response_signature=false and validate_assertion_signature=false. To test insecure defaults, leave both unset/false. To test enforcement, explicitly set the relevant validation flag(s) to true; otherwise acceptance does not prove signature verification occurred.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch, issuer checking is only meaningfully configured when idp_entity_id is set in SAML auth config. If the auth method is configured only with idp_metadata_url, issuer expectations come from metadata; if testing the explicit-config path, the fuzzer MUST set idp_entity_id. Omitting explicit issuer binding in the non-metadata path makes issuer-validation results ambiguous.

SAML login is a 3-step flow in Vault: obtain SSO service URL -> POST SAMLResponse to /auth/{mount}/callback -> exchange token_poll_id + client_verifier at /auth/{mount}/token. A valid I3 flow-coherence test MUST keep token_poll_id and the matching client_verifier/client_challenge pair bound to the same flow. Mixing values across flows will fail by design and is not a security finding.

The ACS callback alone does not return the Vault bearer token. The fuzzer MUST call /auth/{mount}/token after saml_login to obtain session_token. Treating callback success as authenticated success will misclassify incomplete flows as login failures or successes.

For /auth/{mount}/sso_service_url, client_challenge must be the base64-encoded SHA-256 digest of the later client_verifier and must be at least 44 bytes. The fuzzer MUST generate a matching verifier/challenge pair; otherwise token exchange failure is by design, not an I3 issue.

bound_subjects matching semantics are controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, matching is exact string only; wildcards like * are literal characters. If bound_subjects_type=glob, * acts as a wildcard. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST either omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type=glob with an intentional pattern; setting bound_subjects='*' under string mode will only match the literal subject '*'.

bound_attributes matching semantics are controlled by bound_attributes_type, which defaults to string. In string mode, values are exact string matches; wildcard characters are literal. In glob mode, * wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests requiring multiple attribute values to pass, the fuzzer MUST omit bound_attributes or explicitly use bound_attributes_type=glob with intended patterns; do not assume wildcard behavior in the default mode.

bound_attributes accepted values are documented as a single string or comma-separated list of strings. For I5 claim/attribute type-coercion tests, Vault's SAML role constraints are string-oriented; non-string typed values are not documented. The fuzzer SHOULD test numeric coercion by binding a numeric-looking string value and sending alternate lexical forms, but MUST NOT assume native numeric/boolean comparison support.

token_num_uses limits total uses of the issued Vault token, and every API call made with that token consumes a use budget, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if any additional session-authenticated verification calls are included.
Numeric sentinel semantics: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. The fuzzer must not interpret 0 as 'single-use disabled access'; it means no use limit.

Numeric sentinel semantics: token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 in read responses indicate unset/default behavior rather than literal zero-second lifetime. The fuzzer MUST treat 0 as 'inherit mount/system default or disabled field semantics' depending on the field, not as an immediately expired token.

KV v2 pathing is mandatory for secret verification in these docs. The fuzzer MUST use /v1/{engine}/data/{path} for both seed_protected_resource and verify_read_secret. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} is KV v1 and will produce false negatives on KV v2 mounts.

KV v2 engine config sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 means Vault keeps the default 10 versions, not zero versions. delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic deletion timer, not immediate deletion. The fuzzer MUST not interpret these sentinel values as strict-zero behavior.

Identity group aliases require a mount accessor, not a mount path. The supplied docs include group-alias creation but do not include a documented mount-accessor lookup endpoint. The fuzzer must obtain the accessor out-of-band or mark create_group_alias as blocked by missing documented accessor discovery.

External identity groups are intended to receive membership from external aliases. For SAML group-mapping tests, the fuzzer SHOULD use create_identity_group with type='external' and then create_group_alias. Manually populating member_entity_ids on such groups can create misleading authorization results unrelated to SAML group assertion handling.

For I2 SAML freshness tests such as expired assertions or replay, the fuzzer MUST include a control login through the same configured role and flow using a valid assertion first. Otherwise a failed attack login cannot be distinguished from broken SAML setup or mismatched flow state.

For I5 authorization tests involving groups_attribute, Vault uses the asserted group attribute values as names for Identity group aliases created due to successful login. The fuzzer MUST pre-create matching group aliases if it expects group-derived policies to appear; otherwise missing policies are setup errors, not authorization-binding protections.

SAML config trust-anchor inputs are mutually exclusive: either set idp_metadata_url OR set the manual trio idp_sso_url + idp_entity_id + idp_cert. Do not send idp_metadata_url together with manual IdP URL/entity/cert fields.

Vault SAML signature validation is opt-in. validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. For I1 saml_cert_substitution and unsigned/spurious-signature tests, a default-config provider MUST leave these unset/false to test insecure defaults; for enforcement tests, explicitly enable the relevant validation flags.

Issuer validation depends on configuration. idp_entity_id is required only when idp_metadata_url is not used. For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch default-config testing, omitting explicit idp_entity_id in manual config is invalid, so use metadata-based config if you need a setup where issuer comes from metadata; do not assume Vault will compare against an unset manual issuer field.

SAML login is a 3-step flow: obtain SSO service URL -> POST SAMLResponse to /auth/{mount}/callback -> exchange token_poll_id + client_verifier at /auth/{mount}/token. A valid I3 flow-coherence test must keep token_poll_id, RelayState, and client_verifier from the SAME initiated flow; mixing values across flows will fail by design.

The SSO initiation endpoint requires client_challenge to be the base64-encoded SHA-256 digest of the later client_verifier and to be at least 44 bytes long. The fuzzer must generate a matching verifier/challenge pair; otherwise token exchange failure is setup error, not a security finding.
The acs_url supplied to /auth/{mount}/sso_service_url must exactly be one of the configured acs_urls. Using any other callback URL causes login setup failure by design.

token_num_uses limits every API call made with the issued Vault token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. Minimum safe value is 2 if the sequence performs one self-lookup and one protected-resource read; use 3+ if additional session-inspection calls are included. token_num_uses=1 will cause the verification call to consume the only use before the access test.
Numeric sentinel semantics: SAML role token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Do not interpret 0 as 'deny all'; it disables the use-count limit.

Numeric sentinel semantics: SAML role token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 in read responses indicate unset/default/no explicit limit semantics rather than literal zero-second lifetime. Never assume a returned 0 means the token is immediately expired.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay tests, replay the SAME SAML assertion identity material across two full login attempts. Because Vault SAML login is split across callback and token exchange, the second attempt must still use a fresh flow initiation but reuse the same assertion ID in the forged SAMLResponse to test assertion replay handling rather than token_poll replay.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion tests, include a control login with a valid assertion first. A failed expired-assertion login without a successful control cannot distinguish proper expiry enforcement from broken SAML setup.

Vault identity group aliases for SAML group mapping require the auth mount accessor. The provided SAML docs do not document an accessor lookup endpoint, so tests depending on create_group_alias need an out-of-band documented source of mount_accessor or cannot be fully automated from these docs alone.

External identity groups are intended to be populated through aliases from auth methods. For SAML group-mapping tests, prefer type='external' groups plus group aliases rather than manually stuffing member_entity_ids, otherwise the test may not reflect real external-group behavior.

Login enforcement MFA requires at least one scope selector among auth_method_accessors, auth_method_types, identity_group_ids, or identity_entity_ids. A create request with only mfa_method_ids is invalid setup.

For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule tests, MFA enforcement should target the SAML auth mount specifically via auth_method_accessors or auth_method_types including the SAML mount. Otherwise a successful SAML login without MFA may simply mean the enforcement rule did not apply to that auth path.

Vault policy changes take effect immediately by design. For I3 config-change sequences, only flag stale behavior if OLD permissions or OLD trust settings are still accepted after the admin changed them; do not flag successful login/access under the NEW configuration as a vulnerability.
KV v2 verify_read_secret must use the /data/ path segment. Reading /v1/{engine}/{path} would hit KV v1 semantics and produce false failures on a v2 mount.
